To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the activity of calpain in the organs of the mussels, M. edulis L., depends on the content of membrane phospholipids and the activity of Ca2+-channels, which are regulated by membrane phospholipid composition.

the correlation between the activity calpains and content of lipid components of membranes in the organs of Mytilus eduli, is shown in the experiments on the response of mules to the action of Cu2+ and Cd2+.
the activity of calpain is correlated with membrane lipids and intracellular Ca2+ level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of heavy metal action on the activity of intracellu- lar Ca2+-dependent proteases (calpains).
the role of membrane lipid components as the factors that define the functional activity of calpain in the mussel tissues.
the correlation between the content of membrane phospholipids and the activity of calpain in mussels, which is caused by the action of heavy metals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the correlation between the activity and concentration of calpains in mussel tissues is determined by the level of Ca2+ in cells.
the membrane lipid composition of mussel organs is the key factor in the regulation of intracellular Ca levels and, therefore, of Ca2+-dependent processes.
the activity of calpain is determined by the content of membrane lipids, which are the main regulators of Ca2+-channels in the cell membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heavy metals affect membrane lipids and, consequently, the activity of calpain, a Ca2+-dependent protease.

the membrane lipid components of the mussel organs, which are involved in Ca2+-dependent signaling pathways and are responsible for the effector activity, are the most sensitive to the action of the toxicants.
membrane lipid components are the most probable targets for the action of heavy metals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the activity of Ca2+-dependent enzymes is determined by the membrane lipid composition of cells, and the effector activity with respect to Ca channels of membrane lipid components is the most probable mechanism of the correlation between them.

the activity of calpain is a reliable indicator of the physiological condition of mussels, and the level of calpain activity can serve as a biomarker for monitoring the environmental status of the coastal zone.
the correlation of calpain activity with membrane lipid composition is not only observed under the conditions of heavy metal exposure but is also found in mussels living in unpolluted water.
